- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is overly optimistic, apply a downward bias of 3–7% to reflect market caution.  
- Forecasting 30-day ahead: if recent 18-day price trend is downward, model tends to overcorrect upward — suppress early forecast peaks.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/– values), model often overfits short-term noise — smooth forecasts with 3–5 day moving average.  
- When sentiment is consistently above 0.6 over last 5 days, model tends to overestimate future prices — apply a 2–5% downward adjustment.  
- If forecast shows a sharp upward move followed by a steep decline (e.g., 75→70), it often overcorrects — cap the peak and reduce subsequent drop.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–3% of the forecasted value from the last 3–5 days’ average.
